bull_bear.body: Cash & equivalents ~INR 600 Cr; Priority 1: Organic growth (IoT hardware, Govt working capital); Priority 2: Strategic small acquisitions; Dividend: Final FY26 dividend INR 3.50/share (175%); Buybacks not explicitly guided but cash position supports flexibility.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Government payment cycles elongating DSO (Receivables up to INR 176 Cr from INR 133 Cr), though management cites zero bad debt history; Global semiconductor price inflation impacting IoT hardware costs; Execution timing risk on large fixed-price milestones; Macro strain on government finances potentially delaying future tenders.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident in FY27 recovery citing 'positive inflection point' and 'stronger order pipeline'; Transparent on FY26 misses attributing them strictly to customer-side delays (regulatory/fleet readiness) rather than execution gaps; Emphasized fiscal prudence and clean balance sheet despite rising receivables.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Reporting segment restructuring planned for FY27 (Auto/Retail, Corporate, Government) to replace confusing A&M/C&E split; Fixed-price contracts now dominate inflows providing better revenue visibility than volume-based models; IoT hardware costs capitalized on balance sheet create temporary asset bloat but drive long-term high-margin recurring revenue streams.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - The only balance-sheet disclosure is "Cash & cash equivalents (including financial instruments)" of ₹745.3 crore at Q1FY27 against ₹676.9 crore at Q1FY26 and ₹685.0 crore for FY26; the deck sets out no dividend, buyback, capex or reinvestment policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Automotive & Mobility (A&M): +9% FY26, soft Q4 core due to Hyundai variation and delayed IoT fleet rollouts; Consumer & Enterprise (C&E): -3% FY26 due to government deferrals, but +142% QoQ in Q4; Government: Strong recovery in Q4, >INR 200 Cr order book, delayed projects (Energy Response, IoT tenders) pushed to FY27; IoT: Key growth driver, opex model for clients creates fixed asset depreciation on books but high recurring SaaS margins.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Management frames the moat as a usage flywheel: "the more customers use us across different use cases, the more richer our products and solutions become. This is our moat, this is our flywheel".
- Claims a 30+ year build: "we have spent the last 30+ years continuously envisioning the future and innovating at the cutting-edge of tech", producing a "uniquely multi-product, multi-industry and multi-use case company".
- Cites a "rich legacy of having served thousands of enterprise customers across all industry verticals", positioning itself as "an extremely valuable and differentiated digital transformation partner".
- Describes itself structurally as "both an OEM & FDE/Systems Integration Company (combining our OEM products and customer bespoke needs)".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Segment reporting change] From Q1FY27 the company reports market-wise segmental revenue across three customer verticals — Automotive, Enterprise and Government (AEG) — replacing the previously reported A&M and C&E segments, while continuing product-wise Map-led / IoT-led segmental revenue and profitability reporting; FY25 and FY26 history is restated on the new framework.
- [Segment definitions] Automotive covers automotive OEMs (4W/2W/3W and large vehicles across ICE, EV and emerging tech) plus their captive ecosystem and aftermarket; Enterprise covers all private-sector organisations excluding the automotive OEM ecosystem; Government covers all public-sector organisations including Defence, Armed Forces & Police, National Mapping Agencies, Railways and PSUs.
- [Leadership] Rohan Verma appointed Joint Managing Director, subject to shareholder approval, effective 1st July 2026, with responsibility described as including "shaping our Artificial Intelligence roadmap".
- [AI stance] "AI is not new to us. We have been using AI for the last 5+ years to update and enhance our maps"; the company is now "accelerating and increasing our push into AI-native product development, AI-native product offerings and AI-native organizational work".
- [Seasonality] Deck states "Q1 is seasonally weakest quarter for Government business".
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 EBITDA margin 44.6% driven by operating leverage and favorable mix (higher SaaS/IoT); Full-year FY26 EBITDA margin ~16%; Cost mitigation via value engineering offsetting rising DRAM/NAND prices; Inventory build-up is strategic for demand, not speculative gain.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Targeting return to >20% CAGR trajectory in FY27 (vs 1% in FY26) backed by INR 1,750 Cr order book; Margin: Steady-state EBITDA >16% (Q4 demonstrated 44.6% potential via operating leverage), IoT margins expanding via SaaS mix; Order Inflow: Robust pipeline across Govt, Auto, Enterprise; Capex: Organic allocation prioritized for IoT hardware deployment (capitalized) and Govt working capital.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR 1,750 Cr open order book (includes 18% GST); FY26 conversion rate ~18% (INR 270 Cr from opening book + INR 200 Cr from new INR 780 Cr bookings); Composition shifting toward fixed-price milestone and minimum-guarantee models improving visibility; Govt segment alone holds >INR 200 Cr.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Mappls App ecosystem (45M+ downloads, 10M in FY26) expanding beyond navigation to EV, logistics, and safety; Quick-commerce API integration (e.g., Amazon Now) driving enterprise usage; Digital Twin and Defense tech (AR/VR/GIS) opening large sovereign opportunities; IoT fleet scaling compounding SaaS revenues.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: C.E. Info Systems delivered a sharp Q4 inflection (Revenue +54.8% QoQ, EBITDA margin +460bps YoY to 44.6%) driven by the conversion of delayed government and automotive IoT orders, validating the resilience of its INR 1,750 Cr order book despite FY26 full-year stagnation. The strategic pivot toward fixed-price contracts and high-margin IoT SaaS recurring revenue supports a return to >20% growth in FY27, though near-term working capital pressure from government receivables remains a key monitoring metric.

open.item: The Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 3.50 per equity share for FY2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.

The Board appointed Mr. Rohan Verma as Joint Managing Director on June 30, 2026, effective July 1, 2026, subject to shareholder approval, with a mandate to accelerate innovation, develop future-ready technology products and platforms, strengthen strategic partnerships, enhance customer engagement and expand market presence.
The Company enters FY2026-27 with an executable order book and pipeline visibility exceeding Rs 1,750 crore, providing a foundation for future growth.

Continued investment across Maps, IoT, Digital Transformation, AI, Digital Twins and emerging geospatial technologies, and build-out of the Mappls platform into a comprehensive digital location and mobility ecosystem.

The Company will continue investments across Maps, IoT, Digital Transformation, AI, Digital Twins and emerging geospatial technologies to participate in the next wave of intelligent infrastructure and digital ecosystem development.
The Company is entering a new phase of accelerated, platform-led growth via integration of Gtropy, expansion of Mappls DT and global ambitions through Terra Link.
Expand the international footprint through strategic partnerships and subsidiaries, with particular focus on Southeast Asia.
Evolve the IoT segment into a high-margin, recurring revenue business through software-led monetisation and device ecosystem expansion.
Focus technology development on AI-driven geospatial analytics, Digital Twin and simulation technologies, real-time mapping and navigation systems, and integrated IoT and mobility platforms.

Scale Geo-Verify, the AI-powered location verification platform for the banking sector powered by proprietary Geo-LLM technology, and expand across BFSI, e-commerce, logistics, payments and enterprise automation.
Continue investments in innovation and technology as a stated support for sustaining the growth trajectory.
Management flags exposure to global demand fluctuations, capital market volatility and commodity price uncertainties as challenges for the Indian economy.
Management notes temporary moderation in certain geospatial and mapping projects within the Map-led business.
Global economy continues to navigate geopolitical tensions, supply chain reconfiguration and trade realignments, with structural uncertainties embedded in global markets.

The Company states it remains confident of sustaining its growth trajectory, supported by strong order book visibility, expanding customer base, increasing adoption of location-based services and continued technology investment, but gives no numeric guidance.

risks.note: BRSR Q26 (material responsible business conduct issues, with rationale, mitigation and financial implications) is filled 'Nil' across every column, with the explanation 'Given the nature of the business, this is not directly applicable.' A blank materiality assessment means there is no disclosed register of environmental/social risks, mitigations or financial implications for investors to track year on year.
risks.risk: No material ESG/business-conduct risks identified in BRSR — the entire materiality table is returned 'Nil'

risks.note: One of the four stated verticals is Government — central, state and local government organisations, ministries, departments and PSUs — buying geospatial dashboards, GIS health/crime analytics and address-standardisation solutions. Public-sector demand is tender- and budget-cycle driven, making that portion of revenue lumpy and politically/procurement sensitive.
risks.risk: Government/PSU revenue dependence within the customer mix

risks.note: 5,984 customer complaints were filed in FY 2025-26 versus 'Nil' from every other stakeholder group (communities, investors, shareholders, employees, value-chain partners). Resolution improved to almost 99% from almost 95%, but the absolute volume shows the Mappls app / Move IoT retail channel carries a service-quality and brand-reputation exposure that the B2B verticals do not.
risks.risk: High customer-complaint volume concentrated in the consumer/retail channel

risks.note: The only specific commitment disclosed under BRSR Q5/Q6 is a strategic goal of ₹1,000 crore revenue, and the company twice states 'the timeline for attaining this milestone remains fluid' and 'may evolve based on market conditions, business opportunities, and overall economic factors.' An unbounded target cannot be missed but also cannot be held to account, so the growth roadmap is unverifiable.
risks.risk: Execution risk on the ₹1,000 crore revenue goal — an aspiration with no committed timeline

risks.note: Co-founders Rakesh Kumar Verma (Group Chairman & MD) and Rashmi Verma (Executive Director, CTO & CHRO) plus Rohan Verma (Joint MD) hold the executive spine; Rakesh Kumar Verma is also named the highest authority for BRSR implementation. The CTO and CHRO roles are combined in one founder, concentrating both technology and people leadership in a single individual.
risks.risk: Key-person and promoter-family concentration at the top of the structure

risks.note: Permanent-employee turnover ran at 9.39% in FY 2025-26 (9.87% FY 2024-25, 9.75% FY 2023-24) — steady but material for a firm whose asset base is map data and software engineering skill. There are no workers, only employees ('NA' throughout the workers rows), so attrition is the sole labour-side risk channel.
risks.risk: Talent-retention exposure in a pure-IP, people-dependent map/technology business

risks.note: The Risk Management Committee (constituted 27 July 2021) is described as a management-level committee of 4 directors, only half of them Independent, and is chaired by Rohan Verma — described in the same disclosure as a 'Non-Executive Director' while the board list names him Joint Managing Director, an internal inconsistency. Policy review by the Committee and Board is deferred to FY 2026-27, and no external agency has independently assessed the working of the policies.
risks.risk: Governance oversight of sustainability is thinly resourced and internally validated only

risks.note: Women hold 33.33% of Board of Directors seats but 0% of Key Managerial Personnel positions, and female representation is 14.73% of total employees (17.65% of permanent, 11.21% of non-permanent). The gap between board optics and the executive bench is a succession and inclusion watch-item.
risks.risk: Diversity concentrated at board level but absent from executive management
